title: Common Garbage Disposal Problems & Causes
desc: Learn what to do when your garbage disposal jams, hums, or won't turn on and when to call a plumber.

blocks.text: Garbage disposals are convenient appliances that simplify cleanup in modern kitchens. However, they can develop problems over time from normal wear, misuse, or underlying plumbing issues. For many San Antonio homeowners, a malfunctioning disposal creates a major disruption.

Recognizing warning signs early can help you avoid costly plumbing repairs and kitchen chaos. Knowing when you have a serious issue that requires a professional is key to keeping your sink and drains working smoothly.
How a Garbage Disposal Works

Knowing how your garbage disposal works can help you identify what might be wrong. When you flip the switch, a motor spins an impeller plate. Small metal lugs on this plate, called impellers, create centrifugal force, throwing food waste against a stationary grind ring on the chamber’s outer wall. This process shreds food into tiny particles, which water then flushes down the drain.
The Most Common Garbage Disposal Problems
Even a disposal you care for properly may develop an issue. Most problems fall into a few common categories, each with its own set of potential causes and solutions.
Garbage Disposal Won’t Turn On

If your disposal is unresponsive, the issue is likely electrical. First, check for a tripped reset button, usually a small red or black button on the bottom of the appliance. Other causes can include a tripped circuit breaker or faulty wiring. In some cases, a burned-out motor prevents the disposal from turning on.
Garbage Disposal Hums but Doesn’t Work

A humming sound without grinding is a classic sign of a jam. The motor is trying to turn the impeller plate, but something is blocking it. This is often a hard object like a bone, fruit pit, or silverware. In some cases, the motor may have enough power to hum, but not enough to spin the plate.
Slow Draining Sink

When water backs up in your sink, the problem could be inside the disposal or farther down the drain line. A common cause is a clog formed by food waste that wasn’t ground finely enough or a buildup of grease and sludge. Putting the wrong foods down the disposal can quickly lead to a stubborn blockage that prevents proper drainage.
Leaking Garbage Disposal

Water pooling under your sink is a problem that needs immediate attention. Leaks can originate from several places on the disposal. Worn-out seals, particularly the one connecting the disposal to the sink flange, are a frequent culprit.
Connections to the dishwasher hose or main drain pipe can also loosen over time. In older units, the disposal housing itself can crack, causing a leak that requires a full replacement.
Bad Odors Coming From the Disposal

Foul smells almost always result from trapped food particles rotting inside the disposal or in the drain. Over time, a film of food sludge can build up on the internal components of the disposal, creating a persistent odor. Sometimes the smell comes from contamination in the P-trap or the drain line connected to it.
What Not to Put Down a Garbage Disposal
The best way to prevent problems is to be careful about what you put into your disposal. Treating it like a trash can is the fastest way to cause a jam or a clog.

items: Fibrous vegetables like celery or asparagus

blocks.text: Troubleshooting Tips Homeowners Can Try

For minor issues, there are a few safe steps you can take before calling a professional. Always make sure the disposal switch is in the Off position, and then turn off power at the circuit breaker to remove any likelihood of the system accidentally turning on. Either way, never put your hand inside the unit.

items: Check and reset the circuit breaker
Use a flashlight to find obstructions

blocks.text: Signs the Problem May Be in the Plumbing System
Sometimes, a garbage disposal issue is a symptom of a larger plumbing problem. If the trouble extends beyond the disposal, you need a professional to inspect your drain lines.

items: Sink backups after clearing the disposal
Backups into adjacent sinks or the dishwasher

blocks.text: When Repair Makes Sense vs. Replacement

Deciding whether to repair or replace your garbage disposal comes down to several factors. A repair is usually better if your unit is relatively new and the fix is simple. Consider replacement if the appliance is over 10 years old or requires frequent repairs. Replacement is usually the right move if the motor is failing or the repair cost exceeds half the price of a new unit. A new garbage disposal is often more efficient and includes a new warranty.
When to Call a Plumber
Homeowners can do minor troubleshooting. However, many garbage disposal problems require the expertise and tools of a licensed plumber for safe, correct repairs.
